authors: xlix Welcome Message ICSE 2026 Welcome to ICSE 2026 in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil! We are delighted to host the 48th International Conference on Software Engineering for the first time in Brazil, in one of the most vibrant, iconic, and visited cities in the world. ICSE continues to be the premier venue for software engineering research and practice. Hosting ICSE in Brazil and the Global South reinforces its position not only as a globally attended conference, but also as one that is truly globally hosted and co-owned. ICSE 2026 marks a record number of submissions and features a rich and comprehensive program spanning keynotes, panels, multiple tracks, co-located conferences, workshops, tutorials, and symposia. The expanded breadth and depth of the program also reflect the continued growth and impact of software engineering. Despite geopolitical situations elsewhere, we expect to welcome thousands of participants from around the world. For the main conference, ICSE 2026 innovated in the number of keynote speakers and panels, offering six keynote speakers and five panels, carefully curated to address relevant topics and engage with key issues shaping the international research agenda of the software engineering community. The main conference offers a diverse set of high-quality technical sessions. The ICSE program consists of 104 paper sessions (each 1.5 hours), integrating 619 paper presentations from 7 tracks: the Research Track, the Software Engineering in Practice (SEIP) track, the Software Engineering in Society (SEIS) track, the Software Engineering Education and Training (SEET) track, the New Ideas and Emerging Results (NIER) track, the Journal First track, and the Demonstrations track. Beyond these 104 technical sessions, ICSE 2026 features several additional ICSE and pre-ICSE tracks and events, each also including keynotes, papers, and interactive sessions. These include (alphabetic order) the ACM Student Research Competition track, Brazilian Software Engineering Showcase, Doctoral Symposium, Future of Software Engineering track, Industry Challenge track, New Faculty Symposium, Newcomer Activities, Posters track, School of Empirical Software Engineering, Software Architecture BoF, and Student Mentoring Workshop. Furthermore, the program includes two tutorials and seven technical briefings, offering updates on foundational and cutting-edge software engineering topics. We sincerely thank the PC Chairs, Mira Mezini and Tom Zimmermann, as well as all the track chairs, for their tremendous effort and dedication in ensuring that the ICSE program maintains its high quality standards. In addition to the main conference, held from Wednesday to Friday, ICSE 2026 features 10 high quality co-located conferences taking place over the three preceding days and focusing on key topics within software engineering. Each of these conferences offers its own program, including l keynotes, multiple tracks, and paper presentations, with more than 400 papers presented in this context. ICSE 2026 also includes 36 workshops that further broaden the scope of the event, fostering engagement and community building around emerging and specialized topics in software engineering, with more than 300 papers presented. We thank the organizers of the co-located events and workshops for their dedication and contributions to the success of ICSE 2026. Several editorial boards, program committees, and other groups are holding meetings and special sessions at various times, including Tuesday evening and in the latter part of lunch breaks. Check the website for details. Concerning the social program, the conference is held at a beachfront, sustainability certified convention center, and ICSE 2026 offers a variety of social and networking activities designed to foster collaboration and connection. We hope you will take the opportunity to engage with colleagues, exchange ideas, and build lasting relationships. As part of the co-located events program, participants are invited to a social gathering at Rio Scenarium on Monday evening, with buses departing from the conference venue, offering the opportunity to experience one of Rio de Janeiro’s most iconic cultural venues, with drinks and food included. The conference will host a reception on Tuesday at the conference venue, in the main exhibition hall, featuring passed canapés and drinks accompanied by soft live Bossa Nova music, creating a welcoming environment for the community to connect and become familiar with the venue ahead of the upcoming days. The conference banquet will take place at Costabrava Clube on Wednesday and Thursday, a unique venue located on top of a rock overlooking the ocean, offering a memorable setting for an evening of celebration and networking. The experience will feature a curated tasting menu of Brazilian flavors by Pitágoras Leite Gastronomia, the same chef and menu presented during the recent G20 encounter in Rio, along with live Brazilian samba for those in the mood to enjoy the rhythm and atmosphere. Additional networking events are also planned, including a special offsite lunch for the LGBTQ community on Thursday. On Wednesday morning, before the start of the main conference, a yoga session will be held on the beach with Birgit Penzenstadler. The annual ICSE run will take place on Thursday morning along the beachfront sidewalks. Finally, on Thursday afternoon, the traditional soccer game will be held in a beach soccer format, with the possibility of a refreshing dip in the sea after the match. We thank our many sponsors and supporters, including the lead sponsors ACM and SIGSOFT, the IEEE Computer Society and TCSE, our diamond sponsors Huawei and Kunumi Institute, our platinum sponsors IBM and JetBrains, our gold sponsor Cesar School, our silver sponsors AWS, Datamint, Quantum Finance, SBC, and Unico, and our bronze sponsors CEIA, Google, and ZUP Innovation. We also thank our governmental supporters, especially Rio de Janeiro’s State Research Agency (FAPERJ), the Brazilian Research Council (CNPq), and the Rio Convention Bureau (Visit.Rio)
